articles.title: 'I'll be back': vows Kane after ankle surgery
articles.summary: Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return and help his injury-ravaged side for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on h...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return and help his injury-ravaged side for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.

Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle.

Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d'Or winner had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program," Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months.

Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season.

"The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season."

Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: "tough times don't last, tough people do", while thanking his supporters for their messages of support.

Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.

England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England's most capped player's rehabilitation progresses.

England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March.

The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front.

Bayern have been without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer in recent weeks.

On Friday, Michael Olise -- one of Bayern's few remaining forwards -- went down after a tackle late in the first-half.

Despite continuing until the break, the France star did not return for the second-half.

Olise's departure left 18-year-old Germany winger Lennart Karl as the most experienced member of Bayern's forward line, alongside defender Nathaniel Brown, who was moved up to the left wing.

The defending Bundesliga champions did however receive some rare good news on Friday, midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs.

Kompany returned to the dugout with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October.

Musiala came off the bench with 20 minutes remaining in his first appearance in two months.

Diaz is in line to return from injury for Bayern's Champions League match at Lille on Wednesday, while Kompany said early indications suggested Olise's condition was not serious.

"It's just a precautionary measure, I believe," Kompany said. "I'm hopeful Michael will be back Monday."

Bayern remain the last unbeaten team in all competitions in Europe's top five leagues, but Friday's draw means Borussia Dortmund can leapfrog the Bavarians into top spot in the table with a win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.

articles.title: Bayern Munich board decides there’ll be no winter signings
articles.summary: It’s looking like it’s going to be a quiet winter window for FC Bayern
articles.body:
Bayern Munich has already had a bit of an injury crisis so far this season, but it has managed to navigate its way through it by staying at the top of the Bundesliga table, in the top 15 of the Champions League, and through to the round of 16 of the DFB-Pokal.

Prior to the most recent international break, Bayern Munich lost Luis Díaz, Ismael Saibari, and Serge Gnabry to substantial injuries, which mounted on top of Jamal Musiala's long-term injury absence after his medical issues toward the end of preseason. To make matters worse, Manuel Neuer suffered a foot injury just before the international break, and Alphonso Davies picked up a fresh injury while on international duty with the Canadian national team for CONCACAF Nations League matches. All of this—on top of Vincent Kompany's health scare during a training session last month and Joshua Kimmich dealing with the unfortunate loss of his father—has made it a tough road for the German Rekordmeister , but in a way, it has further galvanized a squad that was already displaying an elite level of togetherness that was a huge part of its successes last season.

Despite the number of injuries Bayern Munich has faced so far this season, it does not appear as though there are going to be any depth buys in the January transfer window to help provide more coverage in certain areas of the pitch.

Per information from Bild 's Christian Falk and Heiko Niedderer (via @iMiaSanMia ), FC Bayern's supervisory board made the decision during a meeting earlier this week that the club would not be making any moves in the January transfer window. It will not be making any signings, period. Even with the growing number of injuries and the frequency with which the squad is sustaining injuries to key players, the supervisory board feels that the current squad at Kompany's disposal is good enough to compete across all fronts.

Of course, if any major injuries do arise between now and the winter window, there could be exceptions made à la the club having to go in for Yann Sommer in the winter of 2023 after Neuer's serious leg injury from a skiing accident—bizarre circumstances do happen!

Kompany will certainly be hoping the club's injury luck is far better than it has been in the past two months, though he has had the luxury of a number of players stepping up this season, arguably unexpectedly. Players like Kim Min-jae, Tom Bischof, Konrad Laimer, and Jonas Urbig have had solid seasons thus far, and even Lennart Karl's form has seemingly taken a turn for the better in the past month or so.

articles.title: 'For me, he's a world-class player' - Patrik Schick raves about Bayer Leverkusen team-mate Ibrahim Maza and childhood idol David Beckham
articles.summary: Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrik Schick has hailed 20-year-old team-mate Ibrahim Maza as a world-class talent after forming a strong on-pitch partnership in t...
articles.body:
Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrik Schick has hailed 20-year-old team-mate Ibrahim Maza as a world-class talent after forming a strong on-pitch partnership in the Bundesliga. The 30-year-old forward also reflected on admiring childhood idol David Beckham, admitting the former Manchester United star's global celebrity took him by surprise.

Striker praises young Leverkusen playmaker

Schick reserved his highest praise for sought-after colleague Maza while also looking back on Beckham's career. Signed from Hertha BSC in May 2025 for a reported €12 million until June 2030, the young midfielder has settled rapidly. Maza has delivered three goals and three assists in nine league games, complementing Schick's eight goals and two assists.

Schick highlights strong attacking chemistry

Schick has struck 12 goals and two assists across 15 appearances in all competitions this term, thriving alongside the lively attacker. Discussing Maza's quality and character in an interview with Bundesliga , he said: "I don't need to say much about him on the pitch because he's showing everything himself. Anyone who understands football and watches him play can see that he's unbelievable. I really enjoy playing with him because I think we have good chemistry and understand each other very well on the pitch.

"He's one of those players people should really enjoy watching. On the pitch, he's phenomenal. In the dressing room, he's a very nice guy, a funny guy who's always laughing. Overall, I think he's a great person. For me, he's a world-class player."

Beckham celebrity status surprised Schick

The DFL also quizzed the Czech international about the player who inspired him growing up. Recalling his admiration for the England icon, he said: "It was when I was young. I liked Manchester United, and he was my favourite player at the time. I just really liked the way he kicked the ball, and that was it."

Yet the forward admitted the retired midfielder's commercial rise proved unexpected, adding: "Of course, I didn't know that he would develop into such a big superstar, not just in football but also in marketing and around the world. He's a celebrity. At that time, I simply enjoyed watching him play football."

Leverkusen's attacking duo could soon reunite despite Maza returning early from Algeria duty this month with an ankle issue. Head coach Carles Martinez has indicated the playmaker is expected to be in contention for Saturday's Bundesliga clash against SC Paderborn . Keeping Maza fit and Schick firing will be vital as Leverkusen chase domestic momentum.

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Nada de lo que haga el Real Madrid me preocupa"
articles.standfirst: El técnico alemán analiza el cruce contra el Villarreal
articles.summary: El técnico alemán analiza el cruce contra el Villarreal
articles.body: Hansi Flick valoró el encuentro contra el Villarreal de mañana domingo. El técnico alemán confirmó la baja de Christensen y aseguró que Cubarsí podría, incluso, no entrar en la convocatoria. El técnico alemán no quiso valorar la situación del Real Madrid. Centrales y lesión de Christensen "Yo tampoco lo sé. No tengo aún plan. La situación es diferente de la que cabría esperar. Christensen estaba en un muy buen momento. Decidimos que no fuese con la selección y que se entrenase aquí. Notó algo a principios de semanas y estará fuera dos partidos. En el caso de Cubarsí, no es algo importante pero nos tenemos que preocupar de ello. Veremos si viaja. Koundé está de vuelta y Eric también. Un jugador y medio quedarían fuera. Los grandes clubes de Europa, todos tienen los mismos problemas por la carga de partidos. Hay que gestionarlo todo de la forma más adecuada". Christensen y fichar un central "La lesión de Christensen no afecta, es una situación que conocemos. Hay que ayudarle, que sea consciente de la situación, de que contamos con él cuando está disponible. Está triste porque, cuando está al cien por cien, es uno de los mejores centrales que hay. Cubarsí jugó la temporada pasada una temporada fantástica, un Mundial... y tiene 19 años". Raphinha "Claro que he hablado con él. Tengo mi opinión, pero no es importante. Ellos decidieron lo que decidieron y lo acepto porque es un jugador muy importante para Brasil. Si, cuando está aquí, rinde al cien por cien como lo está haciendo, estoy contento con la situación. Está relajado y listo para mañana". Desgaste de la semana que viene "Forma parte de nuestro trabajo. Es un privilegio también. Jugamos en Champions, para conseguirla, y LaLiga. Pero es nuestro trabajo y nos encanta, a los jugadores también. El entorno del vestuario es increíble. Es increíble ver cómo trabajan todos: médicos, doctores, fisios, utilleros...". Lamine Yamal y la selección "El motivo por el que no jugó el primer partido era claro y todo fue confirmado por parte de la selección. Estoy contento con esta situación. estuvo disponible para el segundo. Así es Lamine. Está a un nivel espectacular e increíble, es fantástico verlo. Estoy muy contento con él". El regreso de Rodri "Hay que esperar. Ver la situación día a día. Pero va bien. La temporada pasada, cuando jugó con el City tuvo una lesión similar. Hoy hablé con él y hay que prestarle atención. No es una lesión tan grave como en el pasado. Tiene buena pinta. Está bien". Sentirse valorado "Mi trabajo es preparar el equipo para que gane. Hemos hecho un buen trabajo, pero on el mejor. No estoy contento con las dos derrotas. Era una semana importante y no logramos jugar al mejor nivel. Me llega que los aficionados están contentos y es responsabilidad nuestra dar el cien por cien por esta gente fantástica y trabajar duro cada día". Dosificar minutos "Otros equipos también tienen que hacer frente a esta situación, pero somos el Barcelona. El objetivo es ganar todas las competiciones pero, al final, hay que ver que tenemos un buen equipo e ir gestionando la carga de minutos. Es importante que todos los jugadores estén disponibles. Iremos recuperando jugadores: Rodri, Cubarsí, Christensen... Olmo ya está de vuelta". De Jong, de lateral "Veremos. Estoy contento con él. Notó una pequeña molestia con la selección, pero está disponible para mañana y eso es lo más importante". Subir el nivel, como dijo Rodri "Por supuesto. Cada día buscamos mejorar, elevar el listón, el nivel... se trata de cada jugador individual y él también tiene que mejorar". Koundé, titular "Veremos. Está disponible. Con las lesiones puedes decir que estará disponible en uno o dos partidos, pero no evolucionó como esperábamos. Le hemos dado el tiempo necesario para recuperarse y volver y ya está disponible". El Real Madrid "Siempre. Ellos, el Atlético, Betis... LaLiga es un campeonato fuerte. No hemos hablado del Villarreal, es un equipo fantástico con un entrenador que tienen un gran futuro por delante. El partido contra el Real Madrid es pasado, ahora nos centramos en el Villarreal. Estamos tres puntos por delante y hay que defender. Nada de lo que haga el Real Madrid me preocupa".

articles.title: Dan Lanning Addresses Controversial Video of Pat Fitzgerald Handshake After Oregon's Win vs. MSU
articles.summary: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning is downplaying any tension with Michigan State's Pat Fitzgerald after the two shared words during the postgame handshake on the field following the Ducks' 45-7 win on Friday night.
articles.body:
Oregon head coach Dan Lanning is downplaying any tension with Michigan State's Pat Fitzgerald after the two shared words during the postgame handshake on the field following the Ducks' 45-7 win on Friday night.

The two coaches met at midfield where Fitzgerald was seen saying something to Lanning, who was able to respond before they went their separate ways.

Oregon Finds Stride With 3rd Straight Win 🔥

Biggest 5-Star Recruiting Busts of Past Decade 👎

Asked about the situation during his postgame press conference (starts at 4:30 mark), Lanning said there were "no issues" between them and praised Fitzgerald as a "phenomenal coach."

Fitzgerald was asked in his postgame media session about Oregon throwing the ball late in the fourth quarter despite having a big lead.

"I'm focused on us trying to play and execute what we need to do and how we need to play," Fitzgerald said . "We don't pick up a fourth-down there at the end, we're trying to score all the way until the end of the game. My focus is on us. We obviously gotta defend those plays. That's on us."

Despite being up by 31 midway through the fourth quarter, Oregon threw four passes on its final offensive possession that accounted for 67 yards.

The Ducks would finish the drive with a one-yard touchdown run from Simeon Price to extend their lead to 38 points with 3:56 remaining.

Lanning's decision to have his offense throwing the ball with the outcome well in hand has led to some criticism that he was trying to build up style points with Oregon on the playoff bubble right now.

In the latest College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday, the Ducks landed at No. 13. They would need to finish in the top 11 to make the field unless they can win the Big Ten championship, but their path to reaching the conference title game would require a lot of things to go right based on tiebreakers.

Oregon even having a chance to make the playoff field is a remarkable turnaround for a team that was 4-3 coming off a 21-10 loss to Illinois on Oct. 24.

Lanning has gotten his team back on track with four straight wins, highlighted by a road victory at Ohio State on Nov. 7.

Oregon will wrap up the regular season on Nov. 28 against Washington at Autzen Stadium.

articles.title: El Alavés resucita sometiendo a un Dépor que sigue de parón
articles.standfirst: Los de Quique rompen dos meses y medio de sequía impulsados por un Boyé estelar, que tumbó con polémica la resistencia gallega tras el gol de Auba
articles.summary: Los de Quique rompen dos meses y medio de sequía impulsados por un Boyé estelar, que tumbó con polémica la resistencia gallega tras el gol de Auba
articles.body: Llegaba muy apretado el Alavés a la cita ante el Deportivo. Seco de victorias desde el 6 de septiembre, los babazorros se sostenían por la mediocridad reinante en la mitad posterior de LaLiga. No se discutía a Quique, pero los picores en Vitoria estaban presentes. El parón se hizo largo. Con esa urgencia doblegaron a un cuadro gallego desdibujado, superado por los tantos de Ángel Pérez y un gran Boyé, y sostenido únicamente por el colmillo de Auba y los guantes de Leo Román. Se aplicaron los babazorros para darle duro de inicio a un Dépor que salió blandito. Blanco olió la sangre, inventó un pase delicioso a la espalda de la defensa y Ángel Blanco lo elevó a obra de arte: control orientado perfecto y misil directo al palo corto. La frustración visitante se tradujo de inmediato en la primera amarilla para Navarro, con un Antonio Hidalgo fuera de sí en la banda ante la apatía del Dépor en el feudo de un rival directo. Por fuera, en largo, a balón parado… Bajo la lluvia, el Alavés sometía a su rival con solvencia, con Rebbach y Toni Martínez perdonando la vida. Era el minuto 20 y el Deportivo besaba la lona. No lo tuvo fácil de salida el Dépor para circular y progresar en Mendizorroza, ya que el Alavés pobló la medular con hasta cinco hombres para morder en la presión y cerrar los espacios interiores a Yeremay, desactivando a un cuadro gallego falto de intensidad. Así, un centro de Quagliata, imposible para Aubameyang, fue lo poco de los gallegos en ataque en la primera media hora. El monólogo del Alavés era absoluto. Boyé rozó la sorpresa desde 40 metros tras robarle la cartera a Casadó y poner en apuros a Leo Román; acto seguido, Rebbach acarició el gol con un disparo cargado de veneno. Perdonar tanto frente a Aubameyang, un juvenil de 37 años, es sinónimo de condena. A la primera que tuvo al espacio, el gabonés dictó sentencia. Superó la presión local con una galopada marca de la casa y sirvió un pase de la muerte que Tenaglia desvió hacia su propia portería. La producción ofensiva de los vascos fue enorme, pero el fútbol entiende de pegada, no de justicia. Apenas se cumplía el primer minuto de la reanudación cuando Rebbach y Toni Martínez ya habían hecho trizas las dos bandas del Dépor, pese a que Hidalgo movió ficha dando entrada a Adama y Giménez para formar con tres centrales. De nada sirvió el retoque: Rebbach pasó de masacrar a Ximo Navarro a someter a Loureiro. Soriano paró un cabezazo de Pablo Ibáñez con la mano tras un córner. Penalti sin duda. Boyé no engañó a Leo Román, que aguantó al máximo; firmó un paradón yendo abajo a la izquierda. No tardó en desquitarse el argentino, aunque con polémica. A los cinco minutos, Boyé tiró de oficio para apartar a Loureiro con un empujón evidente y definir ante Leo Román. García Verdura se llevó la mano al pinganillo, dejó en vilo a Mendizorroza y terminó dando validez al tanto para indignación gallega. Con un Boyé estelar que fue una pesadilla continua, el Alavés jugó con la ansiedad gallega para culminar su triunfo. La sentencia nació tras un jugadón del argentino, que sentó a tres defensas y mantuvo la fe para regalar el gol a Denis. Vuelve a ganar el cuadro de Quique dos meses y medio después ante un rival directo que solo firmó un tiro a puerta. El Deportivo sigue de parón.

articles.title: Diallo present as Africa’s Motsepe reiterates support for FIFA’s Infantino
articles.summary: Africa’s CAF join South America’s CONMEBOL in giving unanimous support of FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election.
articles.body:
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe has said that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Motsepe made the declaration on Saturday in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo, is present.

Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate .

The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat – the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.

CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters, South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL, gave him their “ unanimous ” backing.

CAF has been consistently behind Infantino – who is seeking a fourth and final term – even after the furore he stirred up in July with his short-lived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Morocco is cohosting the 2030 World Cup.

“Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said.

“I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.”

Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, while CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.

Motsepe, though, has been a vocal supporter, and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.

“You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25m to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.

On Wednesday, UEFA Vice President Laura McAllister told the AFP news agency that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.

“He is a Francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said.

McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice president of UEFA, noted that confederations do not vote as a bloc.

“There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said.

“There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.

“This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe; the same rules apply globally.”

articles.title: Jacobo Ramón se viste de Nico Paz y aúpa al Como al top-4 de la Serie A
articles.standfirst: Anotó de cabeza en la primera parte para iniciar el triunfo
articles.summary: Anotó de cabeza en la primera parte para iniciar el triunfo
articles.body: No falló el Como de Fàbregas en el Giuseppe Sinigaglia. Y esta vez, con Jacobo Ramón como incitador del triunfo. El central español, 'de moda' esta temporada, hizo el 1-0 de cabeza ante el Cagliari. Ya en la segunda parte, Da Cunha, otra vez a centro del ex Girona Yan Couto, sentenció el partido. Adelantan al Milan, que tiene un partido menos, y suben al cuarto puesto. No se vio un Como brillante pero el equipo de Fàbregas surfeó el llamado 'virus FIFA' de la mejor forma posible. A los 24 minutos ya ganaba 1-0 en casa ante el Cagliari. Con Nico Paz en el banquillo, descansando tras brillar con Argentina en este parón, el hombre clave fue otro de los jugadores que está brillando en este arranque de curso: Jacobo Ramón. El central español, cuyo futuro será tema de debate en la segunda mitad de la temporada, anotó de cabeza tras un gran centro de Couto. Su cuarto gol esta campaña para el que está siendo uno de los zagueros más prolíficos del curso en Italia. La sentencia llegó ya en la segunda parte, mientras Nico Paz esperaba para saltar al campo en la banda. Una buena jugada, otra vez por la derecha y resuelta con un cabezazo. Esta vez, no obstante, cambiaba uno de los protagonistas: Couto sumó otra asistencia con un centro milimétrico y era Da Cunha el que anotaba. El Como, que se permitió dar espacio a nombres poco habituales como Adrián Lahdo, ya está en 'zona Champions'... a la espera de lo que haga el Milan este domingo.

articles.title: Manchester City 1-1 Fulham: Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi leave Enzo Maresca with Enzo Fernandez dilemma
articles.summary: Manchester City spent £327m overhauling their midfield in the summer - but how does Enzo Maresca find the right balance?
articles.body:
There may have been some eyebrows raised before kick-off when Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca decided to drop club record signing Enzo Fernandez to the bench against Fulham .

Fernandez's lengthy excursions back home to Argentina for their two fixtures during the international break may have been a factor in Maresca's thinking when selecting his starting XI for this game.

If it was, the Italian refrained from giving that as a reason. "I just think for this game it's better having Ayyoub Bouaddi in there," he told TNT Sports shortly before kick-off.

Even so, the move was a significant one as his side were in desperate need of victory after suffering three straight Premier League defeats. That winless streak extended to four after being held to a 1-1 draw.

Maresca had an opportunity to fix the issues in his set-up during the two-week break and admitted on Friday he was searching for "more balance" in the "defensive line, midfield and up front".

The pairing of the steady Bouaddi and all-action Elliot Anderson in the centre of the park was the crucial call, and it may have given Maresca some idea as to how to approach the forthcoming run of games.

"Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good," said Maresca. "Today we used Elliot a bit more attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous.

"It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more as players and also to find the right solution."

Anderson rescues Man City point against Fulham

Anderson steps up, Berge impresses - player ratings for Man City v Fulham

Loud jeers greeted the full-time whistle at Etihad Stadium, a culmination of the feeling that was brewing from the home supporters throughout the game.

There was a nervous tension from the beginning, which seemed to seep on to the players on the pitch.

City displayed a flat first-half performance in which they fell behind courtesy of Rodrigo Muniz's superb curling effort, and they needed a stunning second-half volley from Anderson to rescue a point.

The England international is restricted to sitting in front of the back four when Fernandez is in the side, but has the licence to roam when Bouaddi is deployed beside him.

Aside from scoring a spectacular first Premier League goal for City, Anderson created a match-high three chances and had a 100% success rate from 16 passes in the final third of the pitch.

He also had more touches in the opposition box (7), contested more duels than any other player (17) and no-one else managed to win possession back more times than him.

After dragging his side level, another marauding run into the box was snuffed out by the visiting defenders before Rayan Cherki was brought on, which meant Anderson had to retreat back down the pitch.

Maresca needed to change things in order to apply some fresh impetus in the attacking third, but the substitution of Cherki for Phil Foden seemed to limit Anderson's capabilities.

"It's not a good result, especially off the back of three losses," former City goalkeeper Joe Hart told BBC Sport. "There was some good stuff in there.

"It felt like Elliot Anderson was going to take the game by the scruff of the neck but then Cherki came on and took his position. So he [Anderson] didn't have as much of an impact on the game.

"I understood the change - when the lines are deep, there were chances of Cherki unlocking Fulham , but they just defended so well and they also offered a threat on the break."

'It is important that we find a way to keep clean sheets'

City overhauled their midfield to the tune of £327m with the signings of trio Fernandez, Anderson and Bouaddi.

The £125m club record acquisition Fernandez had made the 14,000-mile round-trip from Manchester to Buenos Aires for Argentina's friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica.

The trip allowed him to take the opportunity to pay a visit to boyhood club River Plate, but it is at his current club where there are question marks as to how he fits into the side.

Bouaddi's presence provides more insurance in front of the defence and the 19-year-old Moroccan has the ability to keep the ball ticking.

It means Anderson can play his natural game - but where, then, does Fernandez fit in?

The number 10 position tends to be occupied by either Cherki or Foden, while Maresca pointed out in his pre-match news conference that City "won games with Enzo and lost games with Enzo".

But the manager clearly has to work out how to get the best out of Fernandez, who was given the final five minutes against Fulham in place of Bouaddi.

"There is no point in having a brilliant squad like Manchester City if you are not going to take that into account," said Hart.

"It's very much understandable, if you're going to have a squad and you trust everyone - if someone's done the travelling, he has done the game time, you have got to expect to not use him as much."

City host Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday followed by a huge trip to Arsenal next Sunday, knowing they could head to the Emirates eight points behind the champions.

Maresca added: "For sure we don't like these kind of moments in terms of four games in a row without a win

"We also know that, unfortunately, it is normal or part of the path, you go through these kind of moments. It is important that we find a way to keep clean sheets that sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference."

Mikel Arteta's men know all about that and City now need to take a leaf out of their book.

articles.title: Falkirk 2-1 St Johnstone: Bairns hold on to beat Saints to extend Scottish Premiership winning run to six
articles.summary: Report as Falkirk beat St Johnstone 2-1; Jacob Murrell opened the scoring with Finley Barbrook doubling their lead; Josh Campbell pulled a goal back for Saints; Falkirk remain third in the Scottish Premiership; St Johnstone are seventh
articles.body:
John McGlynn's team scored early in each half to remain third in the Scottish Premiership.

Jacob Murrell's eighth goal of a superb debut season sent the Bairns on their way inside six minutes and Finley Barbrook's second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage.

Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm thereafter.

McGlynn's well-oiled machine continued to operate at a high level and their surprise bid for a European place shows no sign of stopping.

They went in front when a long Deniss Melniks throw-in was flicked on by stand-in skipper Liam Henderson and Murrell netted on the volley from close range.

Saints created a flurry of chances in response. The pick of them saw Campbell sent clear by Joel Cotterill. The on-loan Hibs forward opted for an early shot and skewed the effort a yard wide.

Top-scorer Josh Fowler found plenty of penalty-box space, too, but his strike was deflected wide.

Falkirk were next to threaten as play swept from end to end.

Toby Steward fumbled a Murrell header from Scott Tanser's delivery but recovered to deny Ethan Ross on his goal line.

Dan Finlayson bravely got his head in the way of a rocket shot from Owen Eames.

Falkirk 'keeper Scott Bain batted away from Taylor Steven and Fowler dragged a great chance wide - both set up by Kai Fotheringham.

Crucially for Falkirk, they were more clinical so close to goal.

Their second, three minutes into the second half, was sparked by Ross feeding Eames out wide. The Derby loan winger's rapid burst of pace did for Liam Smith. Eames fired across goal to award Barbrook with a tap-in from a yard out.

The game should have been over as a contest on 55 minutes but Ross miscued right in front of goal from Murrell's cross.

Simo Valakari made a trio of attack-minded changes, including Danny Schmidt for Fowler.

Within a minute, the German spurned a glorious chance. Campbell's pass was a touch behind the unmarked Schmidt and a weak shot was saved by the legs of Bain.

Falkirk managed the game well until conceding on 83 minutes.

Campbell gave Saints hope by ghosting onto substitute Logan Chalmers' delivery from deep and heading past Bain.

Saints 'keeper Steward joined the attack in the final seconds as a free-kick was launched into the box to no avail.

"I wouldn't have believed it if someone had said we would win six in a row this season.

"We only managed two in a row last season and thought we were doing well.

"To do six is beyond our wildest dreams, really.

"Since coming here, we have always tried to create history and break records.

"That has been unbeaten runs, the 'Invincible' season in League One and games against other teams.

"Winning at Easter Road for the first time in 20 years, beating Celtic for the first time in 19.

"Not many teams have won at Tynecastle recently and we were the first to win there in 18 months.

"We thrive on that. We are always the underdog and we are trying to prove people wrong."

"We didn't give ourselves a chance today. For virtually the whole match we were chasing the game after conceding a goal early in the first half.

"We gifted them a platform and momentum. Then, after conceding a goal early in the second half, it was almost impossible to get back into the match.

"Our players didn't think it was impossible, though. They thought they could do it. But to go 2-0 down away from home against a top team is very hard.

"We are a strong team but we faced a team today that took its chances. We didn't, so we cannot complain."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Kilmarnock 2-4 Aberdeen: Mario Frick makes winning start with Dons as Killie remain bottom of Scottish Premiership
articles.summary: Report as Mario Frick makes a winning start as Aberdeen head coach; Kevin Nisbet scored a double in their 4-2 win at Kilmarnock; the Dons are up to eighth in the Scottish Premiership; Killie remain bottom
articles.body:
Kevin Nisbet's double, coupled with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes, secured three priceless Scottish Premiership points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom.

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where they hit a much-needed scoring streak.

The Dons opted to dispense with the services of boss Stephen Robinson after a run of only one win from seven which saw them sink to second-bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

It should have been advantage to the hosts in the seventh minute as Greg Kiltie picked out Joe Hugill and the striker went one-on-one with Marius Muller but could only rattle his shot into the body of the Dons 'keeper. They were made to pay moments later.

Another slick Aberdeen attack had skipper Nisbet taking full advantage of some familiar hesitancy in the Killie defence to sidefoot a shot into Nico Mantl's bottom left-hand corner and Frick's reign was off and running in emphatic style.

It would get better in the 10th minute as Ieuan Owen was booked for a cynical foul on Nicky Devlin and Nisbet stepped up to brilliantly curl his 20-yard free-kick low past Mantl via post for his 15th goal of the season.

As the Red Army celebrated an astonishing reversal of fortunes, Hicham Mahou rattled a shot in from distance which sailed inches wide of the target as Killie struggled to regroup from the double-whammy but the pulled one back in the 20th minute.

It was a much-needed response as Greg Kiltie reacted first to a loose ball to drive a low shot past Muller and at a stroke the contest was back in the balance.

That would shift again on the half-hour mark as the Dons made it three with Lyons running onto a Nesta Guinness-Walker cross from the left to bury a header past Mantl as the goal-fest continued.

Killie almost reduced the deficit moments after the restart as Michael Schjonning-Larsen's strike was superbly turned away by Muller as the Rugby Park side looked to launch a rescue act.

Manti then blocked a Nisbet shot with his legs as the Scotland international went in search of his hat-trick in the 52nd minute but Kilie were still in the fight and they threw themselves a lifeline five minutes later as Muller gifted possession to Tyreece John-Jules who gratefully accepted by clipping his finish high into the net.

Jamie Brandon squandered a terrific chance to square the game in the 73rd when he blazed a shot over the bar from 16 yards with the goal gaping and with that the Dons held on to see out a contest which allows Frisk to get off to a winning start as the last word went to Marshall who drilled in a fourth three minutes from time.

Mario Frick predicted Kevin Nisbet would get his name on the scoresheet:

"I spoke to Kevin during the week and told him he would score and he scored twice, so he showed how dangerous he is inside the box. He could have scored three but I was very happy for him.

"I can enjoy it now but during the game it was difficult. We were lucky as well as Killie played very well, especially in the second half.

"We had some difficulties but in the end it was a deserved victory. We can defend better as we were lucky, We struggled in the first five or six minutes but after taking the lead we played well. But it was a bit chaotic and I was surprised.

"I told the players to play the way they did when they were young and they didn't think about mistakes or any negatives and played only to win for fun. I told them to play as they did as young players. Watching the third goal was beautiful, it's only the start and a beginning as we need to improve."

Killie boss Neil McCann admitted their winless run has to end, quickly:

"We are just conceding cheap goals and the boys are working so hard in training but when it comes into a game then that's when you really need to execute as that's when it matters most.

"When we managed to get ourselves back into the game at 2-1 I felt that we would go on and create more chances and then we conceded a third.

"In the second half we changed things around a bit as well as some personnel and adjusted how we were playing and I felt from the start of the second half onwards we were the better side.

"We were done on the counter-attack for the fourth goal and when you strip it all down I probably sound like a broken record. but the amount of chances we created and didn't take them....

"It's a sore one as we have worked so hard but it's in games where it matters most and every game is a chance to arrest that."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland: Unai Emery's side held to frustrating draw following tepid performance
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Aston Villa held to frustrating draw against Sunderland at Villa Park; Leon Goretzka and Emi Buendia had half-chances but Villa created very little; Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched late winner for visitors, who remain in Premier League bottom three
articles.body:
Unai Emery's side had 72 per cent possession but failed to make their dominance on the ball count with an expected goals value of just 0.98 xG accumulated.

Opportunities to break the deadlock within the tepid performance were limited to half-chances through Emi Buendia's attempted chip in the first half and Leon Goretzka's shot, which was skewed wide from close range.

Captain John McGinn, who was a shock omission from the starting line-up, sparked a degree of urgency with his introduction at the hour mark and orchestrated the only real goalscoring chance for his side.

The midfielder pulled the ball across the face of goal but substitute Brian Madjo, 17, who had replaced Nicolas Jackson moments earlier, was nowhere to be seen to tap it home.

Sunderland came close to snatching a late winner when Chemsdine Talbi flooded forward on the counter but curled his ambitious shot just wide of the target, to the delight of Zion Suzuki, who was scrambling to meet it.

The point momentarily lifts the Black Cats above Manchester United into 18th, although they remain in the bottom three on goal difference.

For Villa, it was another afternoon to forget as they failed to get back to winning ways after previously squandering a two-goal lead on two occasions at Old Trafford last time out. They sit outside of the top 10 and are winless in their last

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports:

"A little bit frustrated, but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, today was a step forward.

"We were dominating, we were progressing with passes and we were in a good position to control the game, but we didn't create many clear chances.

"Today is not enough, but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward, clear in the style. Keep going forward."

"A good point on the road, absolutely, against a strong opponent. They have many threats everywhere on the pitch, well organised, well coached, good dynamic.

"It was crucial to be solid out of possession, to be able to protect our goal and to manage different threats. In 1v1s, they are so skilled; they can combine in tight areas as well, so the shape we used today was crucial.

"We are a little bit frustrated [with on the ball play] because you have to exploit the opportunities you have but it's just a question of time and confidence.

"Obviously, from the start of the season it was important to switch a little bit. Now we are in the fight really clearly and we have a clear strategy to handle the situation.

"After Chelsea, was it an accident? The answer is no, because we can repeat against another opponent.

"After that, it's a question of just adjusting in transition, the decision-making, the accuracy of the last pass or the last decision. It's a question of time."

Sunderland's game plan works to perfection

The last time these two sides met at Villa Park, it was a seven-goal thriller which included two goals within the final five minutes of regular time and a stoppage-time winner from Tammy Abraham.

This game was the direct antithesis of that game. I have rarely covered a match when absolutely nothing happened but this is one of them.

Sunderland's game plan worked to perfection. They invited the pressure from Villa, denied the likes of Jackson and Manzambi the space they thrive in, and waited for a rare chance to counter. Which almost paid off when Talbi raced forward late on.

Villa lacked a spark throughout this game, which nearly arrived with McGinn's introduction, but when that ball fizzed across the face of goal without a claret and blue shirt to tap it home, Unai Emery likely knew what kind of afternoon it was for his side.

Sunderland secure a point, another building block after their poor start, while Villa will now be tasked with finding that elusive creative spark ahead of their trip to Galatasaray in midweek. There are better atmospheres to try and do that in.

articles.title: Alerta en el PSG: posible lesión grave de rodilla para Doué
articles.standfirst: El jugador galo se lesionó después de hacer el 1-2
articles.summary: El jugador galo se lesionó después de hacer el 1-2
articles.body: Escasos minutos después de firmar el 1-2 y la remontada del PSG en Niza, Désiré Doué se lesionaba de gravedad. A falta de confirmación oficial, el giro de su rodilla, los gestos de dolor y la salida en camilla, con las manos en el rostro, pronostican lo peor para el internacional galo. A pocos minutos para el descanso y antes de hacer contacto con Diop, el jugador del PSG se fue al suelo tras clavar mal la rodilla derecha. Los gritos helaron el estadio Allianz Riviera y el extremo tuvo que salir en camilla, siendo reemplazado por Ferran. Por ahora se desconoce el alcance de la lesión pero las imágenes que dejó la acción no auguran nada bueno. Para el PSG sería un nuevo palo tras la lesión de gravedad de Kvaratskhelia, que se rompió el cruzado semanas atrás. A falta de la confirmación vía pruebas médicas, los peores temores caen sobre la lesión de Doué. "Tenemos que esperar a las pruebas de mañana, pero es una lesión grave, eso está claro", declaró tras el partido Luis Enrique. "Lo hemos podido ver por televisión. Forma parte de la vida de los futbolistas profesionales de alto nivel; vemos situaciones como esta casi cada jornada. Tenemos que aceptarlo. Estoy seguro de que se recuperará muy bien y volverá aún más fuerte. He podido hablar con él; está en el vestuario. Tenemos que esperar a las pruebas definitivas para saber exactamente de qué lesión se trata, pero es una lesión grave", añadió el técnico del PSG.

articles.title: After tumultuous week, Dabo Swinney hits back at critics 'inside and outside' of Clemson following upset win over Duke
articles.summary: Swinney has been the head coach at Clemson since 2009 and has won national titles in both 2016 and 2018.
articles.body:
Clemson head football coach Dabo Swinney has been with the program for 24 years.

The game has admittedly changed over that span, and one of the biggest criticisms of Swinney and the Clemson program was its reluctance to adapt, especially in how it used the transfer portal and NIL.

Clemson pulled off the upset over Duke on Friday night , winning 20-10. Afterward, Swinney held his press conference and took time to call out the media.

"I'm gonna be me. Y'all like for me to come to press conferences and y'all like to ask me all these stupid, antagonistic questions … and trash me. And it hurts. It hurts because I've done nothing but do my best here for 24 years. That's all I've done. Show up every day."

Swinney also called out doubters within the school.

"So many people have quit on our team ... inside and outside of Clemson honestly. But there ain't no quit in our staff, ain't no quit in this football team."

Swinney has faced criticism from sources outside the school, and some within. Clemson wants to evolve with the times, and many wonder whether the school will make the tough call of firing a head coach who won two national titles with the program because of his recent performance and reluctance to fully commit to the new era of college football.

"People wanna get mad because they only wanna look at two years, and that's fair game," Swinney told reporters. "But I've also coached 250 games, and that's fair game, too. I lost my first game and I lost my 250th game, but I'd take Game 2 through Game 249."

After Clemson's loss to Georgia Tech last week, Yahoo Sports' Dan Wolken wrote :

"What we're seeing with Swinney isn't merely about the end of an era at Clemson. It's about the entire concept of the God-tier, statue-worthy coach crumbling as the sport professionalizes. But the gap between where Swinney sits (things are fine, just a rough patch, etc.) and what Clemson sees (this isn't working and a course correction is necessary) is an old tale that has ushered a number of legendary coaches into a retirement they weren't ready to accept."

"What we're seeing with Swinney isn't merely about the end of an era at Clemson. It's about the entire concept of the God-tier, statue-worthy coach crumbling as the sport professionalizes.

But the gap between where Swinney sits (things are fine, just a rough patch, etc.) and what Clemson sees (this isn't working and a course correction is necessary) is an old tale that has ushered a number of legendary coaches into a retirement they weren't ready to accept."

The Tigers' win over Duke on Friday night, plus his response after, feels like Swinney trying to show everyone he still has it — and, most importantly, that he and his team haven't quit. His team will face South Carolina in a rivalry game next week and play in a bowl game to further his point, but Clemson (7-4) still has an interesting decision to make about the program's future.

Swinney was hired as head coach in 2009 and has held the position for 18 years. He spent the six previous years as an assistant coach with the Tigers.

The 57-year-old head coach led Clemson to national titles in 2016 and 2018. He has kept the Tigers among the best teams in the country since, but last year was the first time Clemson had won fewer than eight games in his tenure since 2010.

Clemson's upset win over Duke on Friday night gives it a chance to finish the year 9-4 … but the team could also finish a disappointing 7-6 for the second year in a row.

articles.title: Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
articles.summary: Leeds come from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to shock Chelsea and climb above their hosts to sixth in Premier League.
articles.body:
Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches.

Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart on Saturday by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.

Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London.

Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment.

Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon.

Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period.

Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman.

Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute.

Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home.

Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front.

Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil.

Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool.

While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager.

Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.

Bournemouth and Tottenham on the rise in Premier League

Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game, and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.

Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign.

Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.

Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half.

Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.

articles.title: El Zaragoza sigue con el piloto automático y refuerza su liderato
articles.standfirst: Los maños se impusieron al Rayo Majadahonda con goles de Sangalli y Espiau
articles.summary: Los maños se impusieron al Rayo Majadahonda con goles de Sangalli y Espiau
articles.body: No hay quien pare a este Real Zaragoza. Una victoria más con el piloto automático puesto. Sin una versión brillante ni necesidad de forzar, derrotó al Rayo Majadahonda en el estreno de Carlos Martínez en el banquillo. Sangalli y Espiau anotaron para que los maños ya le saquen seis puntos al segundo clasificado. En la primera media hora apenas hubo nada destacado. Solo en el tramo final antes del descanso se animó el choque. Primero porque los aragoneses hicieron diana en su primer disparo. Rubén Díez abrió a Sangalli que, casi sin ángulo, batió a Prieto. Un golazo del incansable lateral. Los madrileños reaccionaron y llegaron a empatar por medio de Durán pero fue anulado por fuera de juego. Ni mucho menos se podía dar por hecho el triunfo local aunque ya tenían el encuentro cuesta arriba. Los visitantes buscaban el empate en la segunda mitad pero los locales tenían la sentencia en alguna contra. Y en un balón recuperado llegó el tanto que iba a asegurar los tres puntos para los zaragocistas. Tobajas y Cuenca armaron una gran jugada y Espiau solo tuvo que empujar a la red. Todavía quedaban más de 20 minutos pero el choque ya se daba por cerrado. Y así fue. Unos perdieron la fe y los otros no quisieron hacer más daño. Disfruta el Real Zaragoza su mejor momento en muchos años, aunque sea en Primera RFEF. articles.title: Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Noni Madueke grabs Gunners a point after stunning Toon comeback
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Newcastle put on a spirited second-half showing to wobble Arsenal, who lost David Raya to a shoulder injury; Noni Madueke equalised to ensure the spoils were eventually shared
articles.body:
For 45 minutes, this looked like another routine victory for Mikel Arteta's winning machine. Arsenal were dominant, controlling the tempo and suffocating Newcastle with their relentless pressure as Eberechi Eze's opener was exactly what the league leaders deserved.

But football showed yet again it's a game of two halves as Matthias Jaissle produced a tactical masterstroke to change the momentum of the game.

The Newcastle boss made a triple substitution that completely transformed the contest. Suddenly, Newcastle were bolder, braver and playing with intensity.

Harvey Barnes sparked the comeback before Malick Thiaw completed a spectacular turnaround on a night when Bruno Guimaraes returned to St James' Park as an Arsenal player but was withdrawn in the second half after a quiet performance. The first Newcastle captain to lift a trophy in 56 years following their historic 2025 Carabao Cup triumph, he was cheered at full-time when he completed a lap of the pitch.

Arsenal were rattled after falling behind. And their afternoon took another worrying turn when goalkeeper David Raya was forced off with a shoulder injury.

Yet champions find a way to respond and Noni Madueke delivered the equaliser to ensure they escaped Tyneside with a point that extended their lead at the top of the table to six points over second-placed Brighton, who could halve the deficit at Hull on Sunday.

33: GOAL! Eze fires Arsenal ahead as their first-half superiority pays off after a mistake by Lewis Hall.

46: SECOND HALF! Jaissle makes a triple substitution, bringing on Anthony Elanga, Jacob Ramsey and Tino Livramento transforming Newcastle's approach and attacking intent.

49: GOAL! Barnes equalises after Martin Odegaard's error as the momentum swings dramatically.

62: GOAL! Thiaw completes a stunning turnaround, firing Newcastle into a 2-1 lead.

67: INJURY! Arsenal suffer another setback as Raya departs with a worrying shoulder injury.

78: GOAL! Madueke rescues Arsenal with an equaliser to make it 2-2.

Arteta: We lost two points after 'exceptional' first half

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

"But it wasn't. And when it wasn't, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

"And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it's game on.

"And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set-piece.

"And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count."

articles.title: El PSG remonta, Ferran marca... y Doué sufre una posible grave lesión
articles.standfirst: Se teme una grave lesión de rodilla del internacional galo
articles.summary: Se teme una grave lesión de rodilla del internacional galo
articles.body: Felicidad incompleta en Niza para el PSG. Los de Luis Enrique remontaron el 1-0 inicial de Amoura pero, por el camino, perdieron a Doué. Y pinta a lesión grave en la rodilla derecha para el internacional galo. Ocurrió con 1-2 en el marcador, en la primera parte... justo después de que él mismo anotara. Ferran, que entró para reemplazarlo, también marcó para el PSG. Sin el español de inicio, y con un ataque totalmente alternativo formado por Doué, Mayulu y Akliouche, el PSG tiró de remontada en el sur de Francia ante el Niza. Y es que el equipo de la Costa Azul golpeo primero con un tanto al congragolpe de Amoura. El argelino definió bien abajo ante la salida de Safonov. Pero quedó ahí. El PSG era superior, defendió bien su arcó desde ese primera acción terminada con castigo... y fue edificando su remontada. En dos minutos, pasada la media hora, metió dos goles. Primero, Mayulu de penalti; y, ni 60 segundos después, Doué a placer tras una gran jugada de Achraf por el costado diestro. La peor noticia la dejó, precisamente, el internacional galo. Tras marcar se lesionaba y todo apunta a un gravísimo problema de rodilla pues las imágenes que llegaban desde el Allianz Riviera eran terribles. El galo se enganchó la rodilla derecha al buscar un recorte en lo que apunta a una nueva lesión grave de ligamentos... no mucho después de que Luis Enrique ya perdiera a Kvaratskhelia este curso. Salió en camilla, llorando y con las manos sobre el rostro. Ferran entró para reemplazarlo. Fue el español el que hizo un 1-3 que parecía definitivo en la recta final del duelo. Una acción algo enmarañada dentro del área que el ex del Barcelona definió. Pero el Niza, en un arranque de honor, encontró el 2-3 final con Abdi. Un tanto que no cambia nada: los parisinos, líderes en solitario. Para 'Lucho', mientras, son 12 victorias consecutivas entre todas las competiciones: o lo que es lo mismo, la mejor racha de su historia como entrenador superando las 11 consecutivas que logró en Barcelona. Aquel mal arranque de curso ya quedó atrás.

articles.title: Chelsea: Leeds penalty call reopens Premier League handball debate
articles.summary: The decision to give Leeds a crucial penalty in their win at Chelsea reopens the Premier League handball debate around intent.
articles.body:
It is rare when a key handball decision is given for the widespread response to be "that is correct".

Often the discussion centres on the desire for a seemingly more lenient interpretation taking into account perceived intent.

And that is again a talking point after the crucial penalty given against Chelsea in Saturday's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds which ended up putting the visitors ahead for the first time.

Interestingly, despite the perception, handball penalties are much rarer in the Premier League compared with the other top five leagues in Europe.

Last season, there were 22 penalties for handball in the English top flight's 380 games - easily the lowest tally.

Spain's La Liga (36) and Italy's Serie A (38) produced the most.

This season in the Premier League there have been three in 106 matches - less than in 2025-26.

So why was the penalty given against Chelsea 's Morgan Rogers?

'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

The feeling among Premier League clubs is that handball is in a good place now, where the arm must either be fully extended away from the body, raised, or be a deliberate act to be punishable.

And it is the last of these that applied to the penalty given against Rogers, which to some might seem a bit harsh, considering the Premier League's more relaxed interpretation of handball.

There are, however, a few key reasons why referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot, why the video assistant referee (VAR) did not intervene, and why it will be judged as a correct decision.

Two of the factors which a referee looks for when judging a potential handball apply here.

As Jayden Bogle's shot was from distance, a defender is considered to have more time to adjust their body and react - and thus avoid a potential handball.

Most important in this case is the movement of the arm.

When Bogle shoots, Rogers' arm is not raised - but it comes up to the flight of the ball.

Crucially, had Rogers kept his arm in its original position - lower and level with his midriff - there would not have been a handball offence.

What does this mean? Put simply, if the ball would have hit the body if it had not come off the arm, it is considered to have no impact.

But this case was different. Rogers raised his arm and that is what led to the ball being deflected away. This is considered a deliberate act, and this trumps all other considerations.

Perhaps there was a question about whether the ball hit Rogers too high on his arm, and thus should not be a handball offence.

It was close, but it looked like it was in what the laws call the 'red zone', the part of the arm which is punishable for handball.

But this really would be the only reason the VAR, Michael Salisbury, would have any cause to consider an on-field review.

We saw a similar case last season, in terms of how this kind of handball offence is judged - coincidentally involving a penalty awarded to Leeds .

As Anton Stach's powerful strike arrowed towards goal, Everton defender James Tarkowski leaned to his left in an attempt to block the shot - and did so with his arm, which was tucked tightly to the side of his body.

Everton manager David Moyes described the decision as "wrong", but it was absolutely correct in law.

That Tarkowski's arm was close to his side was irrelevant because of the deliberate act of leaning into the path of the ball.

Likewise, Rogers raised his arm to stop the ball and a penalty was a justifiable call.

Decision underlines dissatisfaction with handball law

Despite the Premier League having a more lenient interpretation of the handball law already, it is clear that many observers would like it to go further.

For example, BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer echoed many when he said there should be more intent for a handball.

"I didn't agree with the penalty when Michael Oliver gave it," he said.

"I know once the on-field decision is made there is a high bar to review it, but I don't think officials are allowed to use common sense.

"Morgan Rogers is not deliberately trying to stop the ball. He just doesn't want it hitting him in the face.

"Although the penalty came at an important point in the match, Chelsea were deservedly beaten by a much stronger, far more physical and better-organised Leeds team."

Rogers may argue he raised his arm to protect his face.

This is one of the possible mitigating factors, but usually only applies when a player raises their hands to their face - not using the arm as a barrier.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said that, while he did not "want to make a big thing about it", the penalty should not have been awarded.

"For me it was quite a harsh decision," he told Sky Sports. "I would not have given a penalty. I don't want to make a big thing about it but for me it's not a penalty."

articles.title: Army pranks Navy ahead of annual football matchup with 'Go Army' message in Midshipmen's home stadium
articles.summary: The two service academies have a long history of 'spirit missions' in their rivalry, which has often involved kidnapping mascots.
articles.body:
Army and Navy don't meet in their annual football matchup for another three weeks. But the Black Knights fired a strong opening salvo at their rival service academy with a memorable prank on Saturday.

Prior to Navy's home game versus Memphis at Navy-Marine Corps Stadium in Annapolis, Maryland, Army supporters moved and spray-painted seats in the upper deck that read "GO NAVY" to read "GO ARMY."

Considering those seats are bolted down, rearranging the blue and yellow seats took some time and planning.

The prank was discovered hours before Navy was set to kick off against Memphis at 12 p.m. ET. That provided enough time for staffers — 20 of them, according to ESPN's Morgan Uber — to restore the upper-deck seats to their original message supporting the Midshipmen.

Security cameras viewed the cadets — who were in uniform — moving the seats in the stadium at 1 a.m. ET, The Athletic's Chris Vannini reports . The prank took approximately three hours to complete.

Staffers were dispatched to the stadium around 6 a.m. and took nearly four hours to put the seats back in their original arrangement. But everything was back in its rightful place by the time gates opened to allow fans in at 10 a.m.

Saturday's seat stunt is the latest in a long history of pranks — or "spirit missions," as the two academies call them — between the rival military branches ahead of their annual football clash.

That includes Navy cadets stealing four of Army's mule mascots in 1991. But Navy has had its goat mascot stolen by Army students several times, the most recent attempt in 2021. (However, the wrong goat was stolen in that raid.) A formal agreement was drafted in 1992 to prohibit mascot stealing .

Three years ago, the Midshipmen dropped ping-pong balls with "Beat Army" and "Fly Navy" from three small planes onto the West Point campus.

Air Force has also been the target of pranks from Army and Navy. In 2018, cadets stole a falcon from the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. Yet that prank turned out badly as the falcon injured itself beating its wings against the dog crate it was stored in.

The Midshipmen football team went into Saturday's contest with a 3-6 record (2-4 in the American conference), hosting an 8-2 Memphis squad that has won three of its past four games. That run includes a 49-22 home victory over Army in Week 9.

The Black Knights (5-4, 4-2 conference) take a two-game losing streak into Saturday's matchup with East Carolina (6-4, 4-2). Prior to a bye week, Army lost to Air Force, 24-21 , at West Point.

The 2026 Army-Navy Game will be played on Dec. 12. With the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff format, the matchup could be added to each school's schedule as a 13th game that would be played outside CFP and bowl game consideration.

articles.title: No. 3 Alabama starting backup QB Austin Mack against Chattanooga as Keelon Russell sits
articles.summary: The hope is that Russell gets extra rest ahead of next week's game against Auburn and a possible CFP berth.
articles.body:
The No. 3 Alabama Crimson Tide will be without starting quarterback Keelon Russell on Saturday against Chattanooga. Instead, Alabama will start backup quarterback Austin Mack.

Russell has been dealing with an ankle injury. There were concerns about his availability last weekend against Vanderbilt, but he started and played until the game was in hand. The Crimson Tide offense started slowly but still won 21-6.

Ahead of the game against Chattanooga, Alabama didn't have to submit an official injury report because it was a non-conference game. The assumption was that Russell would get the start, and head coach Kalen DeBoer would look to sit him as soon as possible if the Tide built a big early lead.

Instead, Mack will make his first career start for Alabama. This is his third year with the program. Mack has seen action in 10 total games, including five this year. Overall, in his limited playing time, he is 29-for-39 passing for 290 yards and three touchdowns.

This year, Mack has played largely in garbage time. In five appearances, he has completed three passes for 23 yards.

DeBoer and offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb were both asked about Russell's status earlier in the week.

DeBoer said, "I think, for the most part, he got hit a couple of times, but I think he got through relatively clean. I mean, the injury also wasn't gone completely. So, it's just a matter of managing and kind of see, as the week goes on, where we're at."

Grubb added, "He's doing great. I evaluated him obviously after the game, but yeah, he's doing really well. Right now, I think, status quo, good to go. But again, just big tip of the cap to Austin [Mack]. I think people would have saw how talented a quarterback he is, had he been able to go out there, and he was definitely ready to play."

Russell has played in all 10 games for Alabama so far this season. He has thrown for 2,480 yards with 21 touchdowns and six interceptions. The dual-threat quarterback uses his legs and has added 277 yards and five touchdowns on the ground.

One interesting question is whether it will affect Alabama's CFP ranking next Tuesday. Yes, the Crimson Tide still have to beat Chattanooga on Saturday.

But assuming that happens, the committee will have to rank a top team that sat its starting quarterback to help him get healthier for the end of the season. In the past, teams have been docked for missing their starting playmaker, and it remains to be seen whether the committee would drop No. 3 Alabama.

Russell is expected to be back for the Iron Bowl against Auburn next week.

articles.title: Luca Williams-Barnett: Who is new Tottenham star after goal against Ipswich
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at Tottenham's new teenage star after Luca Williams-Barnett makes a superb full Premier League debut for Spurs
articles.body:
Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".

The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home .

As full debuts go, it does not get much better than that.

Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".

The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.

Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.

They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.

But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.

Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.

"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.

"The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot."

Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.

The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.

Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham 's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.

Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham 's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.

Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.

But this season looks to be his real breakthrough.

Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.

'He's just an incredible football player'

Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.

However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.

His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.

Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.

"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.

"Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing."

The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.

The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.

Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.

"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.

"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.

"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that."

Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.

Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.

"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.

"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.

"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham 's dressing room now is a good environment for him.

"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.

"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."

articles.title: Golazo de Álvaro Martín para que el Castellón duerma líder
articles.standfirst: Un saque de banda favorable al Eldense acaba con un gol orellut desde el círculo central
articles.summary: Un saque de banda favorable al Eldense acaba con un gol orellut desde el círculo central
articles.body: El Castellón ha logrado una victoria trabajada frente al Eldense por 2-0 gracias a los goles Agustín Sienra en la primera parte y Álvaro Martín en el segundo tiempo para alzarse con el liderato de Segunda. Eso sí,. el segundo gol orellut pasará a la historia al marcarlo desde el círculo central. La frialdad e inteligencia de Álvaro quedó patente. Y todo ello, en una jugada que se iniciaba con un saque de esquina favorable a los azulgranas, pero un desajuste hizo que el balón lo controlara Álvaro Martín, quien hizo una jugada personal que acabó en gol. Los albinegros, menos brillantes que otras ocasiones, pero superiores en el global ante un buen rival, han mostrado mucha efectividad en un partido que no tuvieron controlado hasta el segundo tanto, golazo por cierto, anotado en el minuto 87. En una primera parte con pocas llegadas claras por parte de ambos equipos, el Castellón dispuso de la primera ocasión en un disparo desde fuera del área de Orozco que detuvo Ramón Vila. El Eldense replicó dos minutos después con un tiro desde la frontal que paró Matthys. El equipo albinegro estaba espeso en la circulación de pelota ante un rival que presionaba bien y buscaba envíos largos tras recuperación. Pero los de Pablo Hernández encontraron el camino del gol a través de Agustín Sienra, quien recibió de Orozco para batir de tiro cruzado a Ramón Vila. En la segunda parte salió mejor el Castellón, que empezó a circular mejor la pelota y a llegar con más fluidez, pero el Eldense pudo empatar en el minuto 68 en un remate de Nieto que se marchó fuera por poco. Cerca del final, los albinegros acabaron con el suspense a través de Álvaro Martín, que desde el círculo central batió a un adelantado Ramón Vila.
