articles.title: Dundee 0-8 Hearts: Ruthless Jambos return to winning ways with Scottish Premiership demolition at Dens Park
articles.summary: Report as Hearts put eight past Dundee at Dens Park; the Jambos scored four goals in each half; the Dark Blues have Owen Bevan sent off; it was their biggest top-flight victory since 1957; it moves them to within a point of third-place Falkirk
articles.body:
The Jam Tarts went into the game on the back of a run of three straight defeats but they ran riot against the Dark Blues, netting four in the first half thanks to Sabah Kerjota, a Pierre Landry Kabore double and an own goal by Ryan Finnigan.

Dundee were reduced to 10 men after the break with Owen Bevan shown a straight red card before Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Kerjota with his second and Stuart Findlay blew Dundee away with four more goals.

Hearts made the most of their first big chance in the 23rd minute. A long kick-out by Jam Tarts keeper Beau Reus caused havoc, with Dundee defender Bevan trying to clear under pressure from Braga but instead he sent the ball directly to Kerjota, who chested down before clinically firing past Owen Goodman.

And just two minutes later, the travelling fans were celebrating once more. Goodman fumbled a cross with the defence again all at sea before the ball broke to Kabore on the ground and he stabbed home.

Dundee then came close to pulling one back when Westley headed against the bar from a Reilly free-kick.

That was only a temporary respite with Hearts making it three in the 32nd minute when McPake found space down the left and squared to Kabore who gleefully fired past Goodman.

However, the keeper could not prevent Hearts from making it 4-0 in the 40th minute when McPake cut in from the left and hit a shot that took a deflection off Finnigan and flew past Goodman.

The Jambos thought they had made it 5-0 in the 53rd minute when Braga embarked on a great run through the heart of the Dundee defence before firing past Goodman but the goal was ruled out after a VAR check for handball.

Dundee's dismal night then became even worse when Bevan wiped out Braga, with referee Steven McLean brandishing a straight red card.

In the 73rd minute Jordi Altena squared to Braga who rifled home and this time he would not be denied by VAR. Six minutes later, Goodman was picking the ball out of the back of his net again when sub Guendouz cut in from the left and smashed a shot past the keeper.

Hearts made it 7-0 in the 81st minute with Kerjota netting his second with a sweet first-time finish before Findlay well and truly put the icing on the cake eight minutes later, heading past Goodman.

articles.title: Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history
articles.summary: With a ninth successive win, Bournemouth continue to make history under new manager Marco Rose.
articles.body:
"We have to stick together and face reality."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea .

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton , Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea .

"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton .

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."

'I will smile, not just because of the table - because we win'

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth 's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland , Manchester United , Leeds , Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth 's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham .

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth 's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."

It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."

'They should just enjoy what they are doing'

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth 's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

articles.title: Man City stumble again in Fulham draw, Arsenal held by Newcastle
articles.summary: Manchester City's winless Premier League run extended to four games after a damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham, while leaders Arsenal were held to a dramatic 2...
articles.body:
Manchester City's winless Premier League run extended to four games after a damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham, while leaders Arsenal were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.

Third-placed City trail six points behind Arsenal as their title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules.

The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal.

After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca's reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City's quest to topple Arsenal.

Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz at the Etihad Stadium.

City were furious that Erling Haaland's equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno.

Elliot Anderson's sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display.

"Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it's for sure something we need to improve," said Maresca.

At St James' Park, Eberechi Eze put Arsenal ahead in the 33rd minute with a clinical close-range finish from Kai Havertz's pass.

But Newcastle rocked Mikel Arteta's men in the second half.

Harvey Barnes fired Newcastle's 49th-minute equaliser from William Osula's pass after Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard conceded possession cheaply.

When Dan Burn headed down from Lewis Hall's corner, Malick Thiaw pounced to give Newcastle the lead with a 62nd-minute tap-in.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal from only their second league defeat this season, cutting inside for a low drive that eluded Lukas Hornicek's weak attempted save in the 78th minute.

Arsenal are six points above second-placed Brighton, who can close the gap with a win at Hull on Sunday.

"We needed to raise our level in the second half when the opponent had a reaction but we were below the level," said Arteta, who lost 'keeper David Raya to a second half shoulder injury.

"Individually we had some good performances but it was not enough."

Leeds climbed to sixth place after coming from behind to stun Chelsea with a 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny.

Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot.

Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals.

"We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition. Today we were in a fragile moment mentally," Alonso said.

Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries' winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.

Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi's men.

Thomas Frank's arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles' fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.

Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday with the Red Devils second bottom of the table.
